measurement_method: Liu method (log D^2 vs log E from craters); optical microscopy of surface craters
needed_for_model_parameter: F_th_surface [J/cm^2] for surface proxy upper bound
minimum_experiment_type: Single-shot ablation at surface with energy scan
example_sweep: Vary E_p from 0.1x to 10x estimated threshold; measure crater diameter D; plot D^2 vs ln(E); extrapolate to D=0
notes: Must be done on the specific sample batch / surface preparation; surface ablation threshold may vary with polish and coating

measurement_method: Optical microscopy (top-view and cross-section after polishing) of written tracks at varied energy
minimum_experiment_type: Scan writing at fixed depth; energy scan; determine minimum energy for visible continuous track
example_sweep: Vary E_p from 0.5× to 5× estimated internal threshold at fixed depth and scan speed; check track continuity by microscopy
notes: Most important calibration target — enables quantitative threshold prediction

measurement_method: Optical microscopy (top-view) or SEM cross-section; fit width to threshold model D^2 = 2w_eff^2 ln(E/E_th)
needed_for_model_parameter: Track width scaling coefficient; beam-size effective radius at surface
minimum_experiment_type: Energy sweep at fixed scan speed and depth
example_sweep: Vary E_p over range [1x–5x threshold]; measure track width; fit log-linear model
notes: Track width from threshold model requires F_th calibration first (CAL001/CAL002)

measurement_method: Cross-section polishing and optical microscopy; confocal microscopy if available
minimum_experiment_type: Energy sweep at fixed scan speed and depth
example_sweep: Same energy sweep as CAL003; also need cross-section — cut perpendicular to writing axis and polish
notes: Aspect ratio (depth/width) is determined by beam shape; Bessel beam gives very different aspect ratio than Gaussian focus

measurement_method: Optical microscopy (side-view or cross-section along writing axis); check track continuity along z
needed_for_model_parameter: Bessel zone length comparison with Engine 1 prediction
minimum_experiment_type: Scan writing perpendicular to optical axis; image along track direction; confirm z-extent of modification
example_sweep: Fixed energy and speed; vary focus depth to map Bessel zone boundaries
notes: Comparing observed feature length to predicted Bessel zone length validates Engine 1 spatial prediction

quantity_to_measure: track continuity (minimum scan speed for continuous track)
measurement_method: Optical microscopy; check for isolated dots vs continuous track at threshold scan speed
needed_for_model_parameter: Minimum scan speed for continuous modification; N_spot effective for continuity
minimum_experiment_type: Scan speed sweep at fixed pulse energy just above threshold
example_sweep: Vary v from 1 mm/s to 100 mm/s at fixed E_p; measure continuity by microscopy; determine breakpoint speed
notes: Continuity threshold defines the N_spot effective — links scan speed to incubation model

measurement_method: Optical microscopy; DIC; check for secondary ring marks outside main core
needed_for_model_parameter: Side-lobe damage margin — how much energy before secondary ring modifies material
minimum_experiment_type: Energy sweep for each topological charge ell=1 2 3
example_sweep: Fix scan speed; vary E_p; for each ell identify energy at which secondary ring starts to modify material
notes: Critical for vortex-Bessel writing design — sidelobes must not modify material outside intended track

measurement_method: Optical microscopy; DIC; polarisation microscopy for stress birefringence
needed_for_model_parameter: Upper bound on safe writing window; F_th_damage > F_th_modification must be confirmed
example_sweep: Continue CAL002/CAL003 energy sweep to higher energies until crack/void/damage onset observed
promotion_enabled: engine3 uncalibrated → sets upper bound of writing window
notes: Writing window = [F_th_modification; F_th_damage]; if window is narrow writing is difficult

quantity_to_measure: visible microscope contrast (DIC or phase contrast)
measurement_method: Standard DIC optical microscope; phase contrast; cross-polarisation imaging
needed_for_model_parameter: Microscope contrast vs Δn and track morphology; sets simulated_microscopy_proxy calibration
minimum_experiment_type: First written tracks at any condition that produces visible modification
example_sweep: Image same tracks under multiple contrast modes (bright field; DIC; phase contrast; cross-pol)
notes: Knowing which contrast mode gives best visibility informs the simulated image proxy

quantity_to_measure: etch response (etch-rate enhancement at modification sites)
measurement_method: Etch one half of sample in appropriate chemistry (KOH or proprietary ZnSe etchant); measure etch depth and rate by profilometry or SEM
needed_for_model_parameter: Etch selectivity ratio at modification sites; ZnSe etch chemistry
minimum_experiment_type: Apply etchant to laser-modified ZnSe; compare etch depth in modified vs unmodified regions
example_sweep: Etch at a few times and compare etch depth vs exposure conditions
notes: If no etch enhancement exists in ZnSe for these conditions then etch is not a useful observable; this test determines that

measurement_method: Near-field end-face imaging (quantitative phase microscopy QPM); Fabry-Perot fringe contrast; guided mode near field from output
needed_for_model_parameter: Δn magnitude and sign; spatial profile; input to waveguide mode solver
minimum_experiment_type: Write tracks under multiple conditions; measure Δn at each
example_sweep: Vary E_p and scan speed; for each condition measure Δn via QPM or near-field imaging at polished end face
notes: Most critical waveguide-specific parameter; both sign and magnitude needed; negative Δn (depressed cladding) vs positive Δn (smooth modification)

measurement_method: Near-field imaging of guided mode at output end face (butt-couple a laser; image output)
needed_for_model_parameter: Mode field diameter → compare to V-number prediction
minimum_experiment_type: Write waveguide candidates; couple mode; image near field
example_sweep: Try different writing conditions; image mode for each; identify single-mode vs multimode
notes: Combining Δn (CAL011) and mode size gives full waveguide characterisation for V-number model

measurement_method: Cutback method (cleave and measure transmission at multiple lengths); or scattered-light imaging with CCD
minimum_experiment_type: Write waveguides of at least 2–3 lengths; cleave and measure each; compare
example_sweep: Write same condition at 10 mm and 20 mm; compare throughput → slope gives loss
notes: Without propagation loss measurement the waveguide is uncharacterised for application purposes

measurement_method: Profilometry (stylus or optical) of ablation craters; AFM for shallow craters
needed_for_model_parameter: Ablation rate [µm/pulse]; depth scaling with E_p
minimum_experiment_type: Static single-shot ablation energy sweep on surface
example_sweep: Expose at E = 1× to 10× surface threshold; image and measure crater depth
notes: Ablation depth together with CAL001 gives full surface ablation characterisation

measurement_method: Optical microscopy of craters; SEM for sub-µm craters
needed_for_model_parameter: Beam effective radius at surface via Liu method; confirms Engine 1 beam size prediction
example_sweep: Same energy sweep as CAL014; measure D for each energy
promotion_enabled: engine1 optical_prediction validation; engine2 fluence calibration
notes: Crater diameter measurement validates predicted beam size at surface — cross-check of Engine 1

measurement_method: Static multi-pulse exposure (N = 1 to 1000 shots); measure onset fluence for modification at each N; fit to Jee-Becker law
needed_for_model_parameter: S and F_th(1) for Jee-Becker model
example_sweep: Fix spot position; vary N from 1 to 1000 at fixed E; measure minimum E for modification at each N; fit F_th(N) = F_th(1) * N^(S-1)
notes: Most physically meaningful incubation calibration — do NOT borrow S from oxide glass literature
